title: Jony Ive’s first OpenAI gadget is reportedly a hockey puck-sized smart speaker
slides: Why would Jony Ive design a hockey puck speaker?
He is partnering with OpenAI to build it.
The device reportedly lacks a screen entirely.
It prioritizes voice interaction over visual apps.
Your next gadget may listen, not display.
thread_text:
1. Why a puck?

Jony Ive, Apple's design legend, is building a device with OpenAI that has no screen. It's all voice, no visuals.

2. No screen, no apps

This gadget skips the touch interface entirely. Voice becomes the only way to interact, changing how we think about computing.

3. The twist: simplicity

Ive's design pushes back against screen addiction. The device aims to make tech less intrusive, more human, but will it catch on?

4. Big shift ahead

If this works, phone screens could become optional for daily tasks. The AI handles what your eyes currently do, a radical pivot.

5. Test the idea today

Ask yourself: could you replace one app with a voice command? Try it with your current AI assistant and see where it breaks.

instagram.caption:
The next gadget from Apple's design legend reportedly has no screen at all—just voice. Jony Ive is working with OpenAI on a puck-sized speaker that skips visual apps entirely.

The device is built around the idea that you should talk to it, not swipe on it. No display, no touch interface, just conversation as the primary way to interact.

For anyone who creates content, this changes the target. If voice becomes the interface, your words need to work without images or layout to guide them. 🎙️

Could you structure your content to stand alone as a spoken interaction? Try describing your latest piece out loud and see where the gaps show up. 🤔
